stem:
Eshan notices that daytime sunlight makes everything bright, while at night other stars look like tiny points from his terrace.

Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The Sun is the only star; the night points are planets reflecting moonlight.
Other stars look tiny mainly because they are much farther from Earth than the Sun, so their light arrives as points; the Sun is far closer and therefore appears large and bright.
An identical star placed farther from Earth would look larger and brighter than a nearer twin.
The Sun looks large only because it is physically bigger than every other star in the Universe.

teacher.key_rationale: Other stars look tiny mainly because they are much farther away than the Sun.
